notes:
Summary: Enterprise evaluation for Redwood Dedicated. Oakridge builds payments orchestration + fraud/risk services; need predictable throughput for peak settlement windows and sub-50ms token latency on routing model for real-time scoring. Highly cost-sensitive but will pay for guaranteed SLOs and regional residency. Target: 50k TPS embedding/reranking mix during US peak (batch windows) and sustained 5k qps for low-latency scoring; typical request size 128-512 tokens.

Recent timeline: 
- 2026-01-27: Intro call (Maya) — high level needs, asked for capacity planning template.
- 2026-02-18: Deep-dive demo + throughput spreadsheet (ff_2026-02-18_ORP-demo). Covered continuous-batching, KV cache, quantization options.
- 2026-02-25: Security review kickoff (ff_2026-02-25_security-call) — raised data residency + KMS integration. Drive: Security_Questionnaire.pdf submitted.
- 2026-02-28: Internal infra meeting — Oakridge infra team outlined AZ constraints: primary region us-east-1, DR region us-west-2; want <15s failover for stateful caches.
- 2026-03-01: POC planning — agreed to 2-week Dedicated pilot in us-east-1 with representative traffic generator.

Technical requirements / constraints: 
- Throughput guarantees: need reserved pool sized for baseline 4 GPUs (A100xLarge equivalent) per availability zone during business hours + burst pool for settlement peaks. Want hard throughput guarantee for priority routes.
- Latency SLOs: 95th <= 120ms for RLHF-style chat flows; 99th <= 200ms for risk-scoring calls. Must include SLO/penalty language in contract.
- Multi-region capacity: prefer active-primary (us-east-1) + hot-standby in us-west-2. Require cross-region replication of KV cache snapshotting and clear failover playbook.
- Failover headroom: asking for 40% headroom when failing over single region (i.e., remaining region must support 140% of baseline to absorb traffic) — discussion point.
- GPU planning: want SKU guarantees (fp16/qat quant support), ability to pin model variants to smaller GPUs for cost savings.
- Networking: private VPC peering, low-latency inter-AZ path, egress cost cap for DR tests.

Commercial / negotiation points: 
- Committed reserved capacity vs burst billing mix: Oakridge expects committed baseline + metered burst up to X. Pricing elasticity requested for first 12 months.
- SLA discussions: require 99.9% uptime for Dedicated pools and explicit latency SLO credits. Legal asked for sample SLA language.
- Trial: 2-week paid pilot with option to roll into 12-month reserved contract; need price for pilot and conversion credit.

POC plan and metrics: 
- Deliverables: Dedicated pilot in us-east-1 (4 reserved GPUs), routing policy test, autoscaling + burst behavior, KV cache warmup time meas., simulated region failover.
- Success metrics: sustained throughput target (5k qps scoring), 95/99 latency SLOs met, failover <15s with cold-cache performance within 2x baseline, cost per 1k inferences under target.

Notes from calls / quotes: 
- "We cannot accept silent performance variability during settlement windows" — Head of Infra.
- SE asked for detailed multi-AZ worksheet; Oakridge provided internal traffic heatmap (Drive).

Open questions / blockers: 
- Exact GPU SKU availability across us-east-1 & us-west-2 for requested start date (2026-05).
- Confirmation on hot-standby billing model and cross-region egress assumptions.
- Legal needs example SLA with latency credits.
- PO approval timeline — procurement expects calendar Q2 signoff.

Next steps (short): 
- Redwood to return revised regional capacity plan with failover headroom options and pricing tiers (due 2026-03-12).
- Schedule 60-min contract + SLA workshop (legal + procurement) w/ sample SOW.
- Start pilot kickoff once SKU availability confirmed.

Linked artifacts: Drive deck (Regional_Capacity_Model_2026.pptx), Security_Questionnaire.pdf, RINF-4321 ticket for network egress question.

AE notes: keep timeline tight — Oakridge likely to move to procurement if pilot meets SLOs. Focus negotiation on headroom options (40% vs 20%) and SLA credit language.
